class.name: PhysXRiver3D
class.brief_description: A river drawn as a path: a sloped water surface that follows the ground, flows along the path and foams where it is fast or falls.
class.description: Draw the [member Path3D.curve] from the source to the mouth. Each curve point has a width in [member widths] and optionally a depth in [member depths]; the river carries one [member discharge]. [b]Surface.[/b] With [member snap_to_ground], the river measures the static ground under it by raycasts (its bed and its banks). Where no depth is given, the water stands at Manning's normal depth: the height at which the real cross-section, with [member roughness], carries the discharge down the bed's slope. The surface never runs uphill (a running minimum downstream); where the ground drops faster than [member max_slope], the water falls as a cascade. [b]Flow.[/b] The discharge is the same all along the river, so narrows and shallows run fast and pools run slow. Across the channel each strip carries flow in proportion to its depth to the power 5/3 (the divided-channel method), so the deep middle runs fastest and the banks are still. [b]White water[/b] rises where the flow is supercritical (Froude number above about 1) and at the foot of every cascade, and is carried downstream, fading over [member foam_persistence]. The surface is a mesh of its own, drawn with [member water_material]; under path tracing it is a water medium (refraction, depth tint, scattering, caustics), as [PhysXWaterSurface3D] is. A [PhysXBuoyancy3D] whose [member PhysXBuoyancy3D.water_surface_path] points at the river floats on it and drifts with its current.

method.name: clear_sphere
method.description: Stops [param owner] pushing the live water.

method.name: get_carve_brushes
method.description: With [member carve] on, the channel as height brushes for a terrain deformer: one [Dictionary] per square tile of [param tile_size] m (world XZ) the river touches, with [code]rect[/code] ([Rect2], world XZ), [code]cell_size[/code], [code]size[/code] ([Vector2i] cells), [code]heights[/code] (world heights, row-major) and [code]mask[/code] (0 to 1) as [PackedFloat32Array], and [code]mode[/code] ([code]"lower"[/code]: the ground goes down to the height, blended by the mask, never up). Empty when [member carve] is off.

method.name: get_discharge_at
method.description: Discharge (m³/s) at [param s] metres along the river: [member discharge] plus every tributary (a river whose [member mouth_target] is this one) joining upstream of there.

method.name: get_length
method.description: The river's length along its path (m).

method.name: get_live_center
method.description: World XZ centre of the live window.

method.name: get_section
method.description: One cross-section, for tools and tests: [code]centre[/code] (world), [code]s[/code] (m along the river), [code]width[/code], [code]surface[/code] (world height), [code]slope[/code], [code]speed[/code] (mean, m/s), [code]foam[/code], [code]cascade[/code], and per sample across, [code]depths[/code], [code]speeds[/code] (along the river), [code]across[/code] (towards the left bank) and [code]foams[/code].

method.name: get_section_count
method.description: The number of cross-sections (one every [member step_length]).

method.name: get_waterfalls
method.description: One [Dictionary] per waterfall (see [member fall_min_height]): [code]lip[/code] and [code]impact[/code] (world [Vector3], on the bed at the lip and on the pool where the jet lands), [code]height[/code] (m, lip surface to pool), [code]discharge[/code] (m³/s), [code]width[/code] (m), [code]lip_speed[/code] and [code]impact_speed[/code] (m/s), [code]breakup_length[/code] (m of fall after which the sheet is broken into clumps, [code]6 q^0.32[/code] after Horeni) and [code]throw[/code] (m from the lip to where the jet lands).

method.name: is_live_running
method.description: Whether the live window is simulating (its compute solver has started).

method.name: rebuild
method.description: Measures the ground and rebuilds the river now. It rebuilds by itself on the next physics tick after any change.

method.name: sample_depth
method.description: Water depth (m) under a world position; 0 or less off the river or over dry ground.

method.name: sample_flow
method.description: Depth-averaged water velocity (m/s, world) at a world position; zero off the river. It bends round rocks: the flow is a stream function solved over the river with Manning's friction (the diffusive wave), so the water parts in front of a rock, runs faster past its sides and slows behind it. The solve is multigrid-preconditioned conjugate gradients; the project setting [code]physics/physx_3d/water/multigrid_flow[/code] off goes back to the older, slower SOR sweeps.

method.name: sample_foam
method.description: White water (0 to 1) at a world position.

method.name: sample_height
method.description: Water surface height at a world position; [code]-INF[/code] off the river or over dry ground.

method.name: submit_sphere
method.description: A floating body pushing the live water, as [method PhysXWaterSurface3D.submit_sphere]. [PhysXBuoyancy3D] calls it.

members.member: A node with a [code]base_height_at(world_xz: Vector2) -> float[/code] method giving the ground as it was before carving (a terrain deformer keeps those heights). When set, the river reads the ground from it instead of measuring, so once its channel is carved it does not measure the channel and carve deeper on every rebuild. Return NAN where there is no ground.
How far (m) the water mesh reaches past each bank, so the waterline can follow the measured ground.

The river designs its own channel and offers it to a terrain deformer as height brushes ([method get_carve_brushes], [signal carve_changed]): a flat floor [member carve_depth] below the uncarved ground that never climbs downstream (through a rise it cuts), banks sloping up to the ground, and at a bend the deep part moved towards the outer bank. The water then sits in that channel. The river does not change any ground itself.
How steeply (m of rise per m) the carved ground rises again past the banks, where the river cuts through higher ground.
Cell size (m) of the carve brushes; match the terrain's.
How deep (m) the channel's floor is cut below the uncarved ground at the centre.
How far (m) past the banks the brush fades out, so the cut blends into the ground.
Samples across the river, for the ground, the depth and the flow.
The width (m) where [member widths] has no value.
Water depth (m) at each curve point, in order. Empty, or 0 at a point: Manning's normal depth for the discharge there.
Water carried by the river (m³/s). A brook carries 0.1 to 1, a small river 5 to 50.

The waterfalls' falling sheet. Left empty, a built-in shader: a thin slab of water whose streaks ride the falling water, turning white with the air it takes in and breaking into clumps past its break-up length. Its vertex data: UV = (travel time since the lip in s, distance across in m), UV2.x = speed, COLOR.r = edge fade, COLOR.g = aeration, COLOR.b = how far past break-up.

Faces another node draws, as pairs of points (lip, then foot, in global coordinates): the ribbon down each is hidden and no waterfall is made there. [PhysXWaterfalls3D] sets it on every river in the tree for its contact falls.

A drop at least this tall (m), over which the water can fall clear of the ground, is a waterfall: the surface draws down to the brink depth before the lip, the water leaves it and falls as a free jet onto the water below, which boils white. Lower drops, and chutes the jet would run down, stay cascades. 0 turns waterfalls off.

Mist at the foot of each waterfall, drifting out on the air the fall drags down with it: a [PhysXWaterMist3D] per fall, fed with a share of the fall's water that grows with the square of its impact speed, and blown out along the pool at about 0.3 of that speed. In a scene with a [code]PhysXFlow3D[/code] (builds with NVIDIA Flow), a [code]PhysXFlowEmitter3D[/code] feeding it instead.
Scales the mist each fall's [PhysXWaterMist3D] is fed.
Spray thrown up where each waterfall lands: droplets launched at a share of the impact speed (a [GPUParticles3D] made by the river), scaled with the fall's power. Not in the editor.
White water made by the live window where the water runs fast and shears (as [member PhysXWaterSurface3D.flow_foam]); lower than the sea's, since a river runs fast everywhere. 0: none.
Seconds the live window's white water lasts as the water carries it.
Seconds white water lasts as the current carries it downstream.
The physics layers measured as ground. Only static bodies count.
How fast the live part of the flow dies away (1/s). The baked flow never decays.
Side of the live window's square (m).

Run the live window: a square of shallow-water simulation (the solver of [member PhysXWaterSurface3D.live_flow]) round the camera, fed the river's depth and flow. Rocks shed eddies and a meandering wake, and floating bodies swirl in them and disturb the water. The window's mean tilt (the velocity head the baked surface leaves out) is taken out, so only local motion shows. Outside the square the baked flow carries on.
A node the live window follows. Empty: the point on the river the current camera looks at.
Cells along each side of the live window.
Drops steeper than this (m per m) are cascades: the water falls down them instead of flowing.
Metres past the mouth over which the river's surface fades into the water it flows into.

Where the river ends: a lake or the sea ([PhysXWaterSurface3D]) or another [PhysXRiver3D]. The river's surface never falls below that water's level (it ponds back to it), and past the mouth its surface fades into that water over [member mouth_blend]. A lake or the sea gets the outflow as a plume (a turbulent jet spreading from the mouth) that its waves, foam and floating bodies ride; another river carries the added discharge downstream of the join.

Physics layers of rocks and other obstacles in the river, measured on top of the ground. The flow parts round them and white water gathers at them. Needed with [member carve], since a carving river measures the uncarved terrain from [member base_height_source]; without carving, rocks on the [member ground_collision_mask] layers are found anyway.

Raster only: open water mirrors the sky and the sun's glitter by the exact Fresnel term, as the path tracer sees it (the same as [member PhysXWaterSurface3D.raster_reflections]). Off, the surface is the unlit tint it was before.
Manning's roughness: about 0.013 for concrete, 0.03 for a clean natural channel, 0.05 for a stony or weedy one. Rougher rivers run slower and deeper.
Measure the ground under the river by raycasts. Off: the curve is the water surface, and the bed is a parabola [member depths] deep.
Distance (m) between cross-sections along the river.
In the live window, how fast water running along a rock or bank is slowed (1/s). It makes the flow separate behind rocks and roll up into eddies.
The surface's material; created with the river shader if empty. Its parameters set the look in raster and under path tracing.
River width (m) at each curve point, in order. Empty, or 0 at a point: [member default_width].

signal.name: carve_changed
signal.description: Emitted after a rebuild with [member carve] on: the channel's brushes ([method get_carve_brushes]) may have changed.

signal.name: rebuilt
signal.description: Emitted after the river has been rebuilt (its surface, flow and mesh). Rivers flowing into this one listen for it to follow its surface at the join.
